N-alkyl isatin analogs are potent inhibitors of cell proliferation and that their mode of action involves disruption of microtubule dynamics, induction of apoptosis, and G2/M cell-cycle arrest.
N-alkyl substituted isatins are cytotoxic to a variety of cancer cell lines and that this cytotoxicity is mediated via apoptosis.
